systemSummary.name: Cadence Workflow Orchestration Engine
systemSummary.description: Distributed, scalable, durable, and highly available orchestration engine executing stateful workflows and activities with deterministic replay, event-sourcing persistence, and multi-cluster replication.

frontendService.description: Stateless API gateway providing gRPC/TChannel/Thrift interfaces, request authentication/authorization, rate limiting, and domain cache routing.

historyService.description: Core stateful orchestration engine partitioned by ShardID. Manages workflow state machines, mutable state caching, event history append, timer/transfer/replication queue execution, and conflict resolution.

matchingService.description: Task dispatching and queue subsystem. Pairs decision/activity task producers with polling workers using synchronous in-memory channels or persistent task queues.

workerService.description: Internal background worker service hosting system workflows and daemons (ParentClosePolicy, Archival Pump, History Scanner/Reconciler).

storageLayer.description: Pluggable persistence engine supporting Cassandra, MySQL, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, MongoDB for workflow execution/history, and Elasticsearch/Pinot for search/visibility.

durableExecutionModel.eventSourcing: Workflows are persisted as append-only immutable history event streams (history_node / history_tree). State transitions are deterministic projections of event history.
durableExecutionModel.mutableState: In-memory snapshot of execution status, pending activities, user timers, child workflows, and in-flight decisions, protected by shard-level and workflow-level mutexes and synchronized to storage via atomic CAS.
durableExecutionModel.workerExecutionModel: External application workers execute workflow definitions and activities. Decision tasks replay history events to reconstruct local coroutine state. Workflow logic must be deterministic; non-deterministic side-effects must be encapsulated in activities.
durableExecutionModel.optimisticConcurrency: Persistence writes enforce CAS on NextEventID and Shard RangeID. Stale writes fail immediately with conflict errors or shard ownership lost errors.
durableExecutionModel.transactionalOutbox: Side-effects (matching task dispatch, timer triggers, cross-cluster replication, child workflow execution) are staged as transfer/timer tasks within the same DB transaction as history events, then processed asynchronously with at-least-once semantics.
durableExecutionModel.multiClusterReplication: Active-passive domain failover via VersionHistories branch trees. Conflicting histories fork branches in the history tree, and StateRebuilder reconstructs mutable state from the common ancestor.
